title: Multiple Subjects + míg: Compound Historical Sentences

sections.content: Now combine what you've learned so far: multi-subject past narration and the conjunction *míg*, in one compound sentence. This kind of sentence lets you summarize economically but precisely who did what — and what was happening at the same time elsewhere, or with another people.

items.spanish: Míg a rómaiak még Pannóniában uralkodtak, a hunok már a medence keleti részén éltek.
items.english: While the Romans still ruled in Pannonia, the Huns were already living in the eastern part of the basin.

items.spanish: Míg az avarok uralták a medence nagy részét, a szláv csoportok a folyók mentén telepedtek le.
items.english: While the Avars ruled most of the basin, Slavic groups settled along the rivers.

items.spanish: Az avar korszak alatt szláv törzsek is éltek a medencében, míg délen és északon más népek önálló közösségekben éltek.
items.english: During the Avar period, Slavic tribes also lived in the basin, while other peoples lived in independent communities to the south and north.

sections.content: A good compound sentence says two things at once: who did what (subject + past-tense verb), and what happened in parallel (the *míg*-clause). This is exactly the kind of sentence you need to answer clearly: "Who lived in the Carpathian Basin before the Magyars?"
